summary: Sexual-system data for ~23,000 species (Tree of Sex, Dryad CC0), plant selfing-rate compilations and tens of bdelloid genome/read records are public, but none records outcrossing frequency over geological time and no repository holds lineage ages with recombination evidence for putative long-term selfers or asexuals.
next_step: Compile a list of candidate long-term selfers/asexuals from Tree of Sex and the literature, pull their genome assemblies/reads from NCBI, and add divergence ages from TimeTree or the source papers before pre-registering any test.
obstacles_confirmed: 'Unlimited generations' cannot be observed; rare outcrossing is hard to exclude from finite genomic samples.
Tree of Sex records sexual system classes, not selfing rates or outcrossing frequency.
Genomes for most hermaphroditic lineages were not located; only bdelloid counts were queried.
